_comment: TEMPLATE for the DLC-YOLO agent MCP policy, deployed to <app-data>/agent_mcp_policy.json by scripts/setup-crons.py. WHY IT EXISTS: the dlcyolo capability profiles + the orchestrator DECLARE kirocrew-core / kirocrew-cron tools (select_crew, spawn_run, task_run, ask_question, send_message, cron_add) in their agent templates, but a declared tool name is inert unless the MCP server providing it is launched for that agent's session. The app path (kiro_crew.apps.bridges._apply_agent_mcp_policy) does NOT auto-inject the host's managed MCP servers into an app agent; it grants them ONLY via this per-app policy. Without it, every crew-dispatching step (coordinator/builder) blocks with 'select_crew/spawn_run not in inventory' and no crew is ever dispatched. This policy grants the two managed servers (whose launch specs the host resolves via _managed_mcp_spec) to each profile that references them. SEPARATION OF CONCERNS (event-driven-liveness): step-agents / capability profiles are NO LONGER granted cron_trigger — a producer must not poke the scheduler. They write the terminal fact and stop; the app backend's inotify state-file watch wakes the bus (poll is the fallback). Only the orchestrator keeps kirocrew-cron, and only for cron_add/pause/remove to register step-agent sessions — never cron_trigger.
